mission: Quantify wrist-paddle motion synchrony as an ownership signal: correlation/lag metrics between paddle tracks and player wrist trajectories, separability of target-owned vs foreign paddles on the dual-labeled ownership set, and whether synchrony adds discriminative power beyond the current S3 features under a frozen protocol.

method.signal: Per (paddle track, player, wrist): mean per-axis Pearson r between paddle-center velocity and interpolated wrist velocity at lag 0 (best of left/right wrist). Lag scan -333..+333 ms in 67 ms steps recorded as DESCRIPTIVE evidence only; all decisions use lag 0.
method.trackTruth: Gold dual-label candidate points matched to Tier-C paddle tracks within 40 ms and 0.035 normalized units; tracks classified target-owned / foreign / conflicted by matched labels.
frameMethods: s1_synchrony (pure synchrony pick: candidate whose matched track has positive target-vs-others margin)
s2_incumbent_plus_synchrony (incumbent pick kept whenever it answers; synchrony used only on incumbent abstentions)
method.decisionRule: Frozen before measurement: synchrony adds power iff s2 has strictly more correct picks than the incumbent on the same 38 scored frames AND no source-session group loses correct picks.

datasetScopeAndGrouping.split: dev only; loadDualFrames(false, true) with adjudicated E05 corrections applied append-only in memory
datasetScopeAndGrouping.grouping: source-session groups (dvids-944403, dvids-faead, dvids-marne-2024, afn-sasebo-2025-06, wm-tournament-2014); all results reported per group, never pooled per-frame without the per-group table
datasetScopeAndGrouping.dataTier: Paddle detections/tracks and pose are Tier-C machine artifacts (never Gold). Pose provenance disclosed per case: apple-vision (Wave A windows) vs mediapipe-linux-bench (afn-sasebo-rally1, wm-volley-02). No canonical Mac cascade run is claimed or measured here.

holdoutStatement: Held-out cases wm-dink-01 and afn-vic-rally1 were never read, listed, or referenced: they are structurally absent from the SYNCHRONY_CASES registry and loadDualFrames(false, ...) excludes held_out splits.

trackSeparabilityByGroup.note: single-person mediapipe pose gives no foreign-player wrist series; cross-player margin structurally unavailable

findings: Under the frozen rule, synchrony does NOT add discriminative power beyond the current S3 incumbent: s2 correct 28/38 vs incumbent 28/38, with no group improved.
Track-level lag-0 margin separability is near chance on apple-vision groups: target-owned positive-margin 3/7, foreign negative-margin 13/20.
Pure synchrony (s1) is far weaker than the incumbent: 7/38 correct, coverage 13/38 answered (0.342).
s2 raised coverage (abstentions 2 -> 1) but the extra answered frame was wrong, i.e. synchrony converted one honest abstention into an error while net correct picks stayed at 28.

Lag-0 cross-player wrist correlations are uniformly low and mutually similar (typically |r| < 0.3), consistent with common-mode scene/camera motion dominating per-player wrist signal at these paddle-track sampling rates.

MediaPipe linux-bench pose is effectively single-person here, so cross-player synchrony margins are structurally unavailable on afn-sasebo-2025-06 and wm-tournament-2014 (17 of 27 truth-matched tracks abstained). A full measurement of those groups is externally gated on multi-person (Apple Vision / Mac) pose extraction.
Nonzero best-lag values in the descriptive scan are not evidence of a usable lead/lag structure: best-lag scores remain small and inconsistent in sign across tracks.
rationale: The synchrony signal was implemented and measured end-to-end with a frozen protocol on committed dev-only Tier-C artifacts. Measured counts show it neither separates target-owned from foreign paddle tracks reliably (3/7 and 13/20 on apple-vision groups) nor adds correct frame-level picks over the S3 incumbent (28 vs 28 of 38, no group improved). This is an honest negative at current data scale and pose availability; the mediapipe-covered groups remain unmeasurable for cross-player synchrony until multi-person pose exists for them.
productionMutation: Minimal: MethodReport.method / scoreMethod method parameter widened from the MethodId union to string in packages/swing-lab/src/ownershipBench.ts so research method IDs can be scored; no behavior change to the ownership heuristic. New research module ownershipSynchrony.ts, its unit tests, and the own:synchrony script are additive.
